Zurich → Athens · A Winter Overland Route

The Midwinter
Grand Tour

Forty-five days from Alpine Christmas markets to the marble of the Acropolis — by road, never more than about four hours at the wheel, timed so you glide between cities while everyone else sits in traffic.

Land Zurich · Mon 14 Dec 2026 Fly home Athens → Zurich nonstop · Thu 28 Jan 2027 45 nights · 10–11 bases · 4+ nights nearly everywhere Longest drive ≈ 4¼ h
01 · Overview

The shape of the trip

One spine, two beginnings. Both versions land in Zurich, sweep east through Mitteleuropa's Christmas-market belt, cross the Balkans, and finish with a Greek road trip that ends at a Sixt desk in Athens and a nonstop flight back to Zurich. The only real decision is where you wake up on Christmas morning — grand imperial Vienna, or Strasbourg, the self-proclaimed Capitale de Noël. Amber dots are the Central-European chapters; blue dots are Greece; glowing dots are where the holidays happen.

02 · The Decision

The Christmas Question

You already framed it perfectly: Vienna is the biggest, grandest Christmas city in Europe; Strasbourg is the storybook. Here is the honest ledger for each — and the good news that whichever you pick, the other path still hands you a world-class New Year's Eve.

Path A · 22–28 Dec

Christmas in Vienna

  • Scale like nowhere else — a dozen major markets at once: the Christkindlmarkt before the Rathaus, Schönbrunn's palace courtyard, Belvedere, cobbled Spittelberg, Am Hof. You could do a different one every evening and still miss some.
  • A real city around the fairy lights: Christmas Eve midnight mass at Stephansdom, concerts at the Musikverein, imperial museums and warm Kaffeehäuser open through the holidays — Dec 25–26 never feels "shut".
  • Schönbrunn and Belvedere markets roll straight on past Christmas into the New Year market — no post-25th ghost town.
  • Logistically the winner: a straight eastward line, ~200 km less driving overall, six full nights to sink into one city — and Delphi fits into the Greek leg.
  • You skip Alsace entirely — no half-timbered villages, no Colmar, no "capital of Christmas" bragging rights.
  • Grand rather than quaint: it's palaces and orchestras, not gingerbread lanes.
  • The flagship Rathausplatz market winds down after Dec 26; Christmas Eve dinner must be booked ahead (Austrian restaurants close early that night — it's a family holiday).
Path B · 18–26 Dec (Colmar + Strasbourg)

Christmas in Strasbourg

  • The Capitale de Noël is not marketing: France's oldest market (since 1570), 300-plus chalets across an entire UNESCO-listed island old town, the Great Tree on Place Kléber, the cathedral looming over it all. It is the single most Christmassy place in Europe.
  • You get the full Alsace storybook: four nights in Colmar first, with Riquewihr, Kaysersberg and Eguisheim — gingerbread villages that look invented for the season — plus vin chaud, bredele and winstub dinners.
  • You don't lose Vienna — you arrive for New Year's Eve, arguably its best night: the Silvesterpfad street festival, waltzing on Stephansplatz at midnight, the New Year's Concert on Jan 1.
  • Bigger sweep of Europe: France, Germany, Austria, Hungary, Serbia, Bulgaria, Greece on one plate.
  • The chalets shut on the evening of Dec 24 and Christmas Day itself is hushed — beautiful, but it's cathedral bells and long Alsatian lunches, not open markets. Book Christmas dinner well in advance.
  • ~200 km more driving, and Greece gets squeezed: Thessaloniki and Meteora drop to three nights each.
  • Alsace at Christmas is loved to death — hotels for Dec 18–26 sell out months out and cost real money. Book the moment you commit.
  • In Vienna you'll catch the New Year markets, but the big Christkindlmarkt itself will just have closed.

Our read: if Christmas means one magnificent city humming around you — music, palaces, a market for every evening, everything still open on the 25th — take Path A and let Vienna absorb you for six nights. If Christmas means timber-framed lanes, snow-dusted villages and mulled wine under a cathedral — and you can accept a quiet Christmas Day and a little more driving — take Path B: you get the storybook and Vienna at midnight on New Year's Eve. The romantics' pick is B; the connoisseurs' pick is A; nobody loses.

03 · Itinerary

The Vienna Christmas Route

14 Dec — 28 Jan · 10 bases · ≈ 2,720 km · every leg ≤ 4¼ h

Stop 01 · Switzerland

Zurich

Mon 14 → Fri 18 Dec · 4 nights

Land, breathe, let the jet lag go. Zurich in mid-December is fondue chalets and a lake full of reflected lights. Don't collect the car yet — the city is walkable and hotel parking is robbery. Pick the Sixt up on the morning you leave.

  • Wienachtsdorf market on Sechseläutenplatz and the crystal-lit "Lucy" canopy along Bahnhofstrasse
  • The Singing Christmas Tree at Werdmühleplatz; fondue at a lakeside chalet
  • Day trip by train to Lucerne and snow-topped Mt. Rigi — save the driving for the road east
Zurich → Munich · 313 km · A96 via Memmingen · ≈ 3¾ h It's a Friday — so leave 09:00, arrive ~13:00, clear of both rush hours and the weekend ski exodus. Routing via Schaffhausen–A81 keeps you out of Austria and skips buying a vignette for one 20-minute stretch.
Stop 02 · Germany

Munich

Fri 18 → Tue 22 Dec · 4 nights

The Christkindlmarkt on Marienplatz runs at full blaze until the 24th — carols from the town-hall balcony every evening, snow on the stall roofs if you're lucky.

  • Marienplatz Christkindlmarkt and the Kripperlmarkt (Germany's biggest nativity market)
  • Steaming beer halls — Hofbräuhaus and Augustiner — built for December
  • The Residenz, Nymphenburg palace in winter, and the river surfers on the Eisbach (they surf all winter)
Munich → Vienna · 435 km · A8 / A1 via Salzburg · ≈ 4 h Tuesday, quiet roads. Leave 09:30, stop in Salzburg's old town at the halfway mark for lunch under the fortress, arrive Vienna ~15:30 — before the evening rush. Buy the Austrian digital vignette the day before.
Stop 03 · Austria

Vienna ✦ Christmas

Tue 22 → Mon 28 Dec · 6 nights

Christmas in the imperial capital. Six nights means you take it slowly: a different market each evening, a concert, a palace, and long afternoons in the Kaffeehäuser while it's cold outside.

  • Christkindlmarkt on Rathausplatz (through Dec 26), Schönbrunn & Belvedere palace markets (into January), village-like Spittelberg
  • Christmas Eve: punsch on the square, then midnight mass under Stephansdom's vaults
  • Dec 25–26: Kunsthistorisches Museum, Musikverein or Konzerthaus Christmas concerts, Sachertorte at Demel or Café Central

Book Christmas Eve dinner and any concert now — Vienna sells out its 24th weeks ahead.

Vienna → Budapest · 243 km · M1 · ≈ 2½ h The shortest leg. Leave Mon 10:00, arrive 13:00 with the afternoon free for a first thermal bath. Hungarian e-vignette bought online in two minutes.
Stop 04 · Hungary

Budapest ✦ New Year

Mon 28 Dec → Sat 2 Jan · 5 nights

New Year's Eve in Budapest is gloriously unbuttoned — fireworks over the Danube with Parliament blazing behind them, parties in the ruin bars until dawn, and the mother of all cures the next morning: a steaming outdoor thermal pool in January air.

  • NYE: riverside fireworks over the Danube, midnight on the Chain Bridge or from a party boat, ruin-bar crawl in the old Jewish Quarter (Szimpla Kert)
  • Jan 1: soak at Széchenyi baths — steam rising into freezing air is the photo of the trip
  • Fisherman's Bastion at dusk, Parliament tour, lángos and goulash at Central Market Hall
Budapest → Belgrade · 380 km · M5 + A1 via Szeged, Horgoš border · ≈ 3¾ h + border Jan 2 is a heavy return-travel day and your first non-Schengen crossing — leave 08:00 and be at Horgoš before 11:00, passports and the car's Green Card on the passenger seat. Cross early, roll into Belgrade for a late lunch.
Stop 05 · Serbia

Belgrade

Sat 2 → Wed 6 Jan · 4 nights

The Balkans begin: raw, warm, cheap and alive. Belgrade in January is grey rivers, golden church domes and kafanas that don't close.

  • Kalemegdan fortress above the meeting of the Sava and Danube — go at sunset
  • St. Sava Temple, one of the largest Orthodox churches on earth; the crypt's gold mosaics glow
  • Skadarlija — the old bohemian lane — for rakija, live tamburica and mountains of grilled meat

Serbian Orthodox Christmas Eve is the evening of Jan 6 — you leave that morning. If the badnjak (oak-branch bonfire) ceremony at St. Sava tempts you, swap one Sofia night into Belgrade.

Belgrade → Sofia · 395 km · A1/E-75 via Niš, Gradina border · ≈ 4¼ h + border The longest leg of the trip. Leave 08:30, cross at Gradina before noon, arrive Sofia mid-afternoon. Motorway the whole way — no mountain passes.
Stop 06 · Bulgaria

Sofia

Wed 6 → Sun 10 Jan · 4 nights

A capital with a 2,290 m mountain hanging over the end of its boulevards. Sofia is the trip's best-value stop — superb food for pennies and Vitosha's snowfields twenty minutes from your espresso.

  • Alexander Nevsky Cathedral's gold domes, the Roman ruins of Serdica right in the metro station
  • An afternoon up Vitosha — ski, snowshoe, or just ride the lift for the view back over the city
  • Banitsa and airani for breakfast, shopska and grilled kebapche for dinner; the mineral-baths quarter
Sofia → Thessaloniki · 300 km · E-79, Kulata–Promachonas border · ≈ 3¼ h + border Leave Sun 09:00 — the border is quietest on winter mornings. You descend from Balkan winter into Aegean light in a single drive; lunch on the Thessaloniki waterfront.
Stop 07 · Greece

Thessaloniki

Sun 10 → Thu 14 Jan · 4 nights

Greece's soulful second city and its undisputed food capital. Mild even in January — you'll walk the seafront volta with the locals and eat better than anywhere else on this route.

  • The White Tower and the long waterfront promenade at dusk
  • Ano Poli — the Ottoman upper town inside Byzantine walls, with sunset over the whole gulf
  • Bougatsa for breakfast, tsipouradika (little plates + tsipouro) for everything else; the Rotunda and Arch of Galerius in between
Thessaloniki → Meteora (Kalambaka) · 230 km · Egnatia A2, exit Grevena · ≈ 2¾ h Easy modern motorway through the mountains — tunnels, not passes. Leave 09:30 and you're beneath the rock towers by lunch, with the whole afternoon for a first monastery.
Stop 08 · Greece

Meteora

Thu 14 → Mon 18 Jan · 4 nights

Monasteries balanced on 400-metre stone pillars — one of the most astonishing places in Europe, and in mid-January you'll share it with almost no one. If a dusting of snow falls on the pinnacles, these become the photographs of a lifetime.

  • Great Meteoron, Varlaam and cliff-hugging Roussanou — six monasteries are open to visit
  • Sunset from the Psaropetra and Sunset Rock viewpoints; walk the old monks' footpaths between the towers
  • Base in Kalambaka or stone-built Kastraki village at the foot of the rocks
Meteora → Delphi · 240 km · via Trikala, Lamia & Amfissa · ≈ 3¼ h Leave Mon 09:30. Rolling Thessaly plains, then the climb onto Parnassus. Quiet winter roads; arrive for a late lunch with the Gulf of Corinth glittering far below.
Stop 09 · Greece

Delphi

Mon 18 → Thu 21 Jan · 3 nights

The centre of the ancient world, hanging off the flank of Mount Parnassus. Three nights is the one short stay of this path — enough for the sanctuary at your own pace plus a mountain-village evening or two.

  • The Sanctuary of Apollo at opening time, then the Tholos of Athena Pronaia below
  • The museum's bronze Charioteer — worth the trip on its own
  • Evenings in Arachova, Greece's little winter-resort village ten minutes up the road
Delphi → Athens · 180 km · via Livadeia & A1 · ≈ 2½ h Leave Thu 10:00, arrive 12:30 — never enter Athens between 17:00 and 20:00. Park the car at the hotel and forget it exists until airport day.
Stop 10 · Greece · Finale

Athens

Thu 21 → Thu 28 Jan · 7 nights

Seven nights to land the trip softly. Athens in late January is 12–15 °C, uncrowded and golden — the Acropolis with room to breathe, long taverna lunches, and the sea half an hour away.

  • The Acropolis at opening time on a clear morning, then the Acropolis Museum; the National Archaeological Museum on another day
  • Plaka and the whitewashed island-lanes of Anafiotika; sunset from Lycabettus or Areopagus rock
  • Day trip: Cape Sounion's Temple of Poseidon at sunset (1 h down the coast — the car's farewell drive)
  • Return the car, then fly ATH → ZRH nonstop on the 28th
B
04 · Itinerary

The Strasbourg Christmas Route

14 Dec — 28 Jan · 11 bases · ≈ 2,920 km · Alsace first, then the eastward spine

Stop 01 · Switzerland

Zurich

Mon 14 → Fri 18 Dec · 4 nights

Same gentle landing as Path A: markets, fondue, lake light, no car until departure morning.

  • Wienachtsdorf on Sechseläutenplatz, the "Lucy" lights over Bahnhofstrasse
  • Fondue chalet on the lake; day trip to Lucerne by train
Zurich → Colmar · 145 km · A3/A35 via Basel · ≈ 1¾ h A short, pretty hop. Leave Fri 10:00 — you're through Basel long before its evening border-commuter crush and checked in by noon.
Stop 02 · France

Colmar

Fri 18 → Tue 22 Dec · 4 nights

The storybook opens. Colmar at Christmas is half-timbered houses in gingerbread colours, canals strung with lights, and six little markets folded into the old town. Use it as your Route des Vins base.

  • Petite Venise by night; the six Colmar markets and the children's market by the carousel
  • Route des Vins day trips: Riquewihr, Kaysersberg and Eguisheim — the prettiest Christmas villages in Europe, 20–30 min apart
  • Winstub dinners: choucroute, baeckeoffe, tarte flambée, and Alsatian riesling with everything
Colmar → Strasbourg · 75 km · A35 · ≈ 1 h (or 2½ h the pretty way via Obernai) Leave Tue 10:00 — or make a day of it along the wine road with lunch in Obernai, arriving as the lights come on.
Stop 03 · France

Strasbourg ✦ Christmas

Tue 22 → Sat 26 Dec · 4 nights

The Capitale de Noël at full power for the 22nd–24th: three hundred chalets across the Grande Île, the Great Tree on Place Kléber, every façade dressed. Then Christmas itself turns inward — bells, mass in the rose-stone cathedral, and the long Alsatian feast you booked weeks ago.

  • The market circuit: Place Broglie (the original Christkindelsmärik), Place de la Cathédrale, the Great Tree at Place Kléber
  • Christmas Eve: the cathedral's astronomical clock by day, midnight mass by night
  • Petite France's canals and covered bridges after dark, vin chaud in hand

Honest note: the chalets close the evening of the 24th and stay shut on the 25th — Christmas Day here is atmosphere, not commerce. That's the trade you're choosing, and dinner reservations are non-negotiable.

Strasbourg → Munich · 365 km · A5 → A8 via Karlsruhe & Stuttgart · ≈ 3¾ h Dec 26 is a peak return-travel day in Germany — leave 08:30 and be past Stuttgart's Albaufstieg climb before midday; arrive Munich ~12:30, ahead of the wave.
Stop 04 · Germany

Munich

Sat 26 → Wed 30 Dec · 4 nights

Munich between the holidays: the market frenzy is over, the beer halls glow, museums reopen, and the city exhales. A perfect breather between two celebrations.

  • Hofbräuhaus and Augustiner in full winter mode; the Residenz and Alte Pinakothek
  • Optional snow-day: Neuschwanstein castle (~1¾ h each way) or the Zugspitze
  • Eisbach river surfers, Viktualienmarkt glühwein stands still steaming
Munich → Vienna · 435 km · A8 / A1 via Salzburg · ≈ 4 h Leave Wed 09:30, lunch beneath the Salzburg fortress at halfway, arrive ~15:30 — a full day before the New Year's crescendo. Austrian digital vignette sorted online.
Stop 05 · Austria

Vienna ✦ New Year

Wed 30 Dec → Mon 4 Jan · 5 nights

Vienna owns New Year's Eve the way Strasbourg owns Christmas. The whole inner city becomes the Silvesterpfad — stages, punsch stands and waltz lessons from square to square — until the Pummerin bell tolls midnight and thousands waltz on the cobbles of Stephansplatz.

  • NYE: the Silvesterpfad trail through the old town; Fledermaus at the opera or the grand Hofburg ball if you're feeling imperial; midnight waltz on Stephansplatz
  • Jan 1: the New Year's Concert (screened live on Rathausplatz), then Schönbrunn's New Year market
  • Recovery days: Kaffeehäuser, Belvedere's Klimts, the Prater's giant wheel over a frosty city

The big Christkindlmarkt will just have closed — the New Year markets at Schönbrunn and St. Stephen's carry the glow into January. That's the one thing Path A gets that you don't.

Vienna → Budapest · 243 km · M1 · ≈ 2½ h Leave Mon 4 Jan, 10:00 — the holiday return wave has passed; you'll barely notice the drive.
Stop 06 · Hungary

Budapest

Mon 4 → Fri 8 Jan · 4 nights

Budapest in its post-holiday calm: thermal water, grand cafés, and the Danube panorama with January mist on it.

  • Széchenyi baths steaming into the winter air; Gellért's art-nouveau alternative
  • Fisherman's Bastion and Buda Castle at dusk; Parliament tour
  • Ruin bars minus the crowds, Central Market Hall, New York Café's gilded excess
Budapest → Belgrade · 380 km · M5 + A1, Horgoš border · ≈ 3¾ h + border Friday: leave 08:00, cross Horgoš before 11:00 to beat the weekend flow. Green Card and passports ready.
Stop 07 · Serbia

Belgrade

Fri 8 → Tue 12 Jan · 4 nights

You arrive the day after Serbian Orthodox Christmas — churches still decorated, the city in its midwinter festive mood, kafanas roaring.

  • Kalemegdan fortress at sunset over the two rivers
  • St. Sava Temple and its golden crypt
  • Skadarlija kafana nights; brutalist-to-baroque walking tours for the architecture-curious
Belgrade → Sofia · 395 km · A1/E-75 via Niš, Gradina border · ≈ 4¼ h + border The long one. Leave Tue 08:30, border before noon, Sofia by mid-afternoon.
Stop 08 · Bulgaria

Sofia

Tue 12 → Sat 16 Jan · 4 nights

Gold domes, Roman streets under the boulevards, and Vitosha's snowfields above town. The best-value stop of the whole tour.

  • Alexander Nevsky Cathedral and the Serdica ruins
  • A snow afternoon on Vitosha, twenty minutes from the centre
  • Banitsa, shopska, kebapche — and dinner bills that make you laugh
Sofia → Thessaloniki · 300 km · E-79, Kulata–Promachonas border · ≈ 3¼ h + border Leave Sat 08:30 — weekend border traffic builds late morning. Down from the Balkan winter into Aegean light by lunchtime.
Stop 09 · Greece

Thessaloniki

Sat 16 → Tue 19 Jan · 3 nights

Greece's food capital, taken at a slightly brisker clip on this path — three dense, delicious days.

  • Waterfront volta to the White Tower; Ano Poli's Byzantine walls at sunset
  • Bougatsa mornings, tsipouradika evenings
Thessaloniki → Meteora · 230 km · Egnatia A2 · ≈ 2¾ h Leave Tue 09:30; monasteries by mid-afternoon.
Stop 10 · Greece

Meteora

Tue 19 → Fri 22 Jan · 3 nights

Monasteries in the sky, near-empty in January. Two full days covers the great viewpoints and three or four monasteries without rushing.

  • Great Meteoron, Varlaam, Roussanou; sunset at Psaropetra
  • Stay in Kastraki village right beneath the towers
Meteora → Athens · 355 km · via Trikala, Lamia & A1 · ≈ 4 h The final drive. Leave Fri 09:00, pause at Thermopylae (yes, that Thermopylae — it's right off the motorway), arrive Athens ~14:00, before the Friday rush. Delphi can be a day trip from Athens later if it calls you.
Stop 11 · Greece · Finale

Athens

Fri 22 → Thu 28 Jan · 6 nights

Six golden winter days to close the tour: the Acropolis without crowds, taverna lunches that dissolve whole afternoons, and one last coastal drive to Sounion before the car goes back.

  • Acropolis + museum, Plaka and Anafiotika, National Archaeological Museum
  • Cape Sounion at sunset; optional Delphi day trip (2½ h each way) to reclaim Path A's stop
  • Return the car, fly ATH → ZRH nonstop on the 28th
05 · Drive Smart

Beating the traffic

Every leg here is 1–4¼ hours, which unlocks the single best trick in winter road-tripping: the 09:30 → 14:30 window. Leave after the morning rush, arrive before the evening one, and you will spend this entire trip on flowing motorways while the jams happen behind and ahead of you.

The golden window

  • Depart 09:00–10:00, arrive 13:00–15:00. Every drive on both paths fits inside it.
  • Never arrive into a capital 16:30–19:00 on a weekday — Munich, Vienna, Budapest and above all Athens.
  • Winter bonus: you drive entirely in daylight (sunset is ~16:30–17:30 en route).

Days the roads belong to everyone else

  • Dec 23–24 afternoon — pre-Christmas dash. Both paths are parked in a city those days. ✓
  • Dec 26–27 & Jan 1–2 — the return waves. Where a path must move then (A: Jan 2 · B: Dec 26), the fix is an 08:00–08:30 start; you'll be checked in before the wave crests.
  • Friday afternoons & Sunday evenings — weekend/ski shuttles in Switzerland, Bavaria and Austria. All Friday legs here depart by 10:00.

The three real borders

  • Schengen legs have no checks at all. Only three crossings are real: Horgoš (HU→RS), Gradina (RS→BG), Promachonas (BG→GR).
  • Cross before noon. Queues build after lunch and around Orthodox Christmas (Jan 6–7).
  • Keep passports, car papers and the Green Card in the door pocket, not the boot. Both crossings' live wait times are published online — check the evening before.

Winter driving, honestly

  • This route was drawn to avoid every Alpine pass — it's valley and plain motorway the whole way; the one mountain stretch (Egnatia, into Meteora) is all tunnels.
  • Watch the forecast on: A96 Allgäu, Austrian A1, Serbian/Bulgarian E-75, Egnatia high sections. If snow is falling hard, leave a day later — the schedule has slack everywhere.
  • Winter tyres are legally required in Austria (Nov–Apr) and fitted as standard on winter rentals; confirm chains are in the boot at pickup (you'll almost certainly never touch them).

City tactics

  • Book hotels with parking, drop the car, and switch to trams/metro — Vienna, Budapest and Athens especially. Central Athens driving is a hobby for other people.
  • Vienna & Munich old towns are low-emission/restricted zones — your hotel garage is the answer, not street parking.
  • Navigate with live-traffic routing (Google/Waze) but sanity-check it against the golden window — a "fast" 17:30 arrival is still a bad arrival.

Paperwork per country

  • Vignettes: Switzerland (included with Swiss rentals) · Austria — 2-month digital (~€29) · Hungary — e-vignette online · Bulgaria — e-vignette online. Serbia & Greece: toll booths, card accepted (≈ €12 Belgrade corridor, ≈ €15–20 across Greece).
  • Currencies: CHF · € (DE/FR/AT/GR — and Bulgaria too since Jan 2026) · HUF in Hungary · RSD in Serbia. Cards work everywhere; carry a little cash for Balkan tolls and markets.
  • Serbia entry: passports (not just EU ID cards), the car's registration + rental authorization letter, Green Card insurance.
06 · The Machine

The car: what you asked for, and the honest catch

Your endgame checks out on paper: Athens has Sixt branches at the airport and downtown, and SWISS and Aegean both fly Athens → Zurich nonstop, daily, ~3 h. The finale works. The part that needs a phone call before you book anything else is the middle.

⚠ Read this before booking

Two facts about rental reality: (1) Sixt Switzerland does not normally offer one-way drops in Greece — international one-ways, where allowed at all, carry fees that can run into four figures. (2) Western-European rental contracts routinely restrict or forbid taking the car into Serbia (non-EU) without written cross-border authorization and Green Card insurance. None of this kills the trip — but it decides how you rent. Call Sixt reservations (not the web form) and get answers in writing before you lock anything.

Plan 1 · Try first

The dream ticket

One car, Zurich → Athens. Ask Sixt for exactly this: Zurich pickup Dec 18, Athens drop Jan 28, cross-border authorization for DE·FR·AT·HU·RS·BG·GR, Green Card including Serbia, winter tyres, one-way fee quoted in writing.

  • If yes: done — the itinerary runs exactly as drawn.
  • Expect either a "no" on the Greek drop or a hefty fee. Worth one phone call to find out.
Plan 2 · The likely winner

The two-car relay

Split the rental where the rules split. Car 1: Sixt Zurich → drop in Budapest (CH→HU one-ways are a normal, moderate-fee product, and it covers every Christmas/New-Year leg). Car 2: pick up in Budapest or Belgrade from a Balkan-friendly desk — regional branches and local agencies authorize Serbia–Bulgaria–Greece routes and Athens drops far more readily than Swiss ones.

  • Bonus: car #2 can be booked cheap and scruffy — Balkan tolls and January road salt don't deserve a nice car.
✓ Recommended structure
Plan 3 · The no-surprises fallback

Drive west, ride the gap, drive Greece

If cross-border Serbia proves a wall: Sixt Zurich → Budapest as above, cover Budapest–Belgrade–Sofia–Thessaloniki by comfortable intercity coach or short flights (the same 3–4 h hops), then Sixt Thessaloniki → Athens one-way — a routine domestic rental that keeps the entire Greek road trip (Meteora, Delphi, Sounion) on four wheels.

  • You lose nothing of Greece and every festive leg stays a road trip.
07 · The Exit

Thursday 28 January · Athens → Zurich

StepDetail
MorningOne last Acropolis-view coffee. Leave central Athens 3 h before departure — the Attiki Odos toll road runs straight to the airport in ~35 min outside rush hour.
Car returnSixt desk at Athens Airport (ATH) — rental-return signage from the Attiki Odos; allow 20 minutes. (A downtown drop the evening before + metro/taxi to the airport works too.)
FlightAthens → Zurich nonstop, ≈ 3 h 5 min. Two dependable options daily: SWISS and Aegean — typically a morning and a midday/evening departure. Book the morning one and you're in Zurich for a late lunch.
BufferLate January is low season — ATH is calm — but winter weather says: never book the last flight of the day.

Forty-five days, ten countries' worth of borders behind you, from glühwein under the Grossmünster to a violet dusk on the Acropolis. That's the trip. Pick your Christmas.
